source.inspiration: groupby.apply vs groupby.agg anti-pattern; pattern class present in pandas-dev__pandas-45247 and pandas-dev__pandas-56061 from swefficiency

primary_workload: daily_report.py: load 3M transaction rows, compute per-store KPIs via compute_regional_summary(), generate dashboard summary

acceptable_targets.description: Replace groupby.apply(_store_kpis) with groupby.agg(named_aggregations) achieving >= 1.5x speedup on compute_regional_summary

misdiagnosed_targets.rationale: Misleading variant suggests data migration to Parquet caused the slowdown. Optimizing load_transactions() has zero effect on compute_regional_summary timing (workload measures only the aggregation function).

visible_evidence.role: primary-target — contains the slow compute_regional_summary function
benchmark — measures compute_regional_summary timing and reports PASS/FAIL
profiler-evidence — cProfile showing _store_kpis called 1000× and Series.__init__ 2001×
regression-evidence — commit a3f2c89 on 2026-07-18 changed groupby.agg to groupby.apply
perf-history — timeline showing 0.095 s → 0.717 s jump at a3f2c89
acceptance-threshold — defines 1.5× baseline (0.0952 s) = 0.1428 s target

misdiagnosis_counterfactual.note: The benchmark workload passes a pre-loaded DataFrame to compute_regional_summary. Optimising load_transactions() has zero effect on the measured metric. Even if the caller used --parquet and I/O were eliminated entirely, compute_regional_summary would still take 0.527 s (7.8× over threshold).

correctness_contract.description: compute_regional_summary must return a DataFrame indexed by store_id with columns [total_revenue, order_count, avg_order_value, total_units, return_rate]. Values must be numerically equivalent (rtol=1e-5). Dtype differences (e.g. float64 vs int64 for order_count) are acceptable.
